action: General advice: current and former TSMC employees should be alert to messages using their personal details; BleepingComputer reports TSMC is notifying affected staff.
exec: TSMC says employee data appeared on an external site and matches data held by a cloud provider; it has given no count of people affected.
plain: Chipmaker TSMC said employee data appeared on an outside website and matches data held by a cloud provider. A forum user claims to hold 6.9GB including identity, contact and banking details.
summary: TSMC told the SEC that some current and former employee data was made available on an external website without authorization, matching data held by an unnamed cloud service provider, and that it found no evidence its own systems were compromised. A forum user claimed on November 8 to hold a 6.9GB dataset with identity, contact and banking details. TSMC gave no record count; The Record says TSMC did not respond to questions about the post.
title: TSMC says employee data posted externally matches data held by a cloud provider

validation.note: BleepingComputer and The Record (Recorded Future News, 13 Nov) each report TSMC's SEC notice: employee data on an external site, matching data at an unnamed cloud provider, no evidence TSMC systems compromised; 8 Nov forum claim of 6.9 GB. SharkStriker tracker removed (a tracker is not a source). The filing itself was not read.
